In the evening Fehmi Lladrovci and several of his comrades came and told us that we had to merge with the Celiku staff. After several discussions Ymer and friends agreed. And the unit was called number 3, Celiku 3."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now on the version, on what you're reading from it says "Celiku 3" and this is at the bottom of 6994.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it. That is what is written down there. Of course, when I made the description that day, it couldn't have been like that, but later on I must have added Celiku 3 because at that time there was no such name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that you didn't learn -- you weren't given the name Celiku 3 until the meeting with Celiku a few days later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour I would just note than the translation it just says Celiku. Celiku 3 does not appear but it appears on the original document which is attached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Forgive me for interrupting, I'm so sorry. It's on the same point and on the same sentence. When the witness read it in Albanian what we have in English at page 8, namely "I signed as well," certainly didn't appear in my headphones and on our screens as well. I see Your Honours agreeing with me. I wonder if my learned friend would ask the witness just to read Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that last sentence again so we can check whether it should or should not be "I signed as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Certainly. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you just read on that entry for the 12th of May, 1998, could you just read the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: "I also signed and thus the Lapusnik post got the name Celiku 3." But as I said, it was not on that day that it was called Celiku 3. It was only called the Celiku unit, but after two or three days, it was given the number 3 when Celiku came and held that speech in Lapusnik. It could have been written on the day when the name -- when we got that name, but it -- when I wrote these notes or when I -- it got the name, Celiku 3, but it was not on the day that -- the 12th of May, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now other than that -- aside from that clarification about Celiku 3 is -- is what's written here accurate about what you remember occurring that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Very accurate. But the number 3 is not accurate in relation it that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Now, if you could just look at the entry for the 14th of May, and I'm not going to ask you to read it out loud. But if you could just read through the entry for the 14th of May to yourself.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that an accurate account of what you remember occurring on the 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could turn now to the 21st of May, which is on page 6996 of the Albanian, page 9 of the English translation. And if you could read the first two sentences.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: "At around 10.00 in the morning, four friends from Klecka arrived as reinforcements. They had one mortar, one 50 millimetre and one machine-gun."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that happen on the 21st of May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last sentence says -- as we have it translated it says Kaki [phoen] and I had already finished working on the position, the bunker, and we had isolated it with nylon because of the rain." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, who is the person Kaki that is referred to there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Albanian spoken] Kaki. I apologise. It is Kaki and his -- it's the short form for Isak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the position that is referred to, what position is that, the position or bunker?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It is position 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had you finish the working on it on -- by the 21st of May?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, it was covered because of the rain. It had been covered also with branches, thick branches. But we also worked on it later and reinforced it later. All the time, all the time that we were in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could turn to the next page, which is an entry for the 29th of May, 1998. And it's on 6997 of the original. Can you just take a moment - it's rather long so I'm not going to read the whole thing, but if you could just take a moment and read through it and tell us if it is an accurate account to your memory to what occurred -- or some of the things that occurred on that date.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Would you like me to read it aloud?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You can just read it to yourself for the moment.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it an accurate account of some of the things that happened on the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, very accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a few specific things that are in that entry. At the beginning it says that "You were at the position you had been working on that Voglushi and Qerqiz got there as well." And then it says, "Qerqiz who was the person in charge ordered me to fire at the first member of the infantry which had already approached us." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes that is how it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Qerqiz the person in charge?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It later says -- and this on page ten at the top of the translation. I can't say precisely where it is it on the Albanian original -- but it says that you "only had one radio at the Staff and could only communicate with the other positions by word of mouth." Is that right, did you have one radio?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, just one, a small one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of radio it was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It was a radio with a small capacity. These things you can buy in Kosovo now everywhere are very cheap. It was not professional. I think only five kilometres or ten kilometres of range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where -- was the radio kept at any particular place in the position of Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: No. Qerqizi kept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It then says that -- you're describing some events and it says "At that moment I heard the voices of 'Qerqiz' and 'Voglushi' telling me to withdraw." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is later a reference to Timi and Zenel. Do you know who those people were?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. They were soldiers who had come a few days ago from Klecka, but now they were staying in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know their true names at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: No. No, not then, not now. I know that Timi was killed. I think that his name was Fatim and he was called Timi for short. Zenel is Zenel, a name, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is then a sentence which reads in our translation it says, "The commander Fatmir Limaj ('Celiku') took the 500 millimetre mortar," or I believe it says the mortar 500, "and a local soldier and told him how to approach the tank." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened. Somebody had brought that day a mortar. It was hand-held mortar. It was a 500 metre range and not five millimetre as a calibre. And that's what they took in order to eliminate or to annihilate that tank that was stuck in the mud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've testified that you wrote these entries into that book from notes and that you wrote -- wrote them in that book in August or September of 1998. Do you remember when you wrote notes, how long after the 29th of May you wrote notes about what happened on the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I am sure that the events of the 29th of May, I wrote down about them on the 30th of May. There was time enough for me to write because there was no fighting. Perhaps towards the evening of the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then did you use those notes when you wrote that entry in that book?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: From the other notebook the same things I wrote down in this notebook. I tried to keep a chronological order here but I later understood that it was impossible to write down all of the things chronologically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this exhibit be given a number and placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P169, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We're going to put a copy of the Albanian and the translation into evidence. The witness would like to keep the original diary. Of course, the Defence can have full opportunity it review the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure that that is done and no difficulties then that it would be with everybody's concurrence that the exhibit itself, the original itself, might be returned as long as everyone is content with the copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Given a opportunity to look at the original, I'm sure it can be returned, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that is a convenient time, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think is as well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, before the break you described how positions 1 and 2 were created. After the end of May 1998, were other fighting positions created in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: After the battle of 20 [as interpreted] May, the number of soldiers in Lapusnik increased. I said that they came from Lladroc unit along with many volunteers. The number was approximately over 60. Therefore, it was necessary for us to dig up other trenches, positions. And three more were built. The number increased to five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now in the translation it said the battle of the 20th of May. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It was the 29th of May. I said the battle of 29th of May. After that battle, three new positions were built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where in Lapusnik those three additional positions were?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Beginning from Guri, which was position number one, then position number two, in that direction, towards the mountains of Berisa, three new positions were built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the battle of the 29th of May, what were your duties in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I had the same duties. We dealt mainly with people who came in that direction. There was a road that led to the position. We stopped them, we asked them why were they there. Most of them came wishing to join the KLA units. And that's it, more or less. This is what we did. We were dealing with digging of trenches and this -- the villagers helped us in digging these trenches up to position number four and five. They were connected with each other, these positions. We built other positions. In position number two, we dug two other positions so there were three bunkers altogether in position number two in June and July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you stay in position number two during the months of June and July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. Until the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that people would come to the position number two along the road and that most of them were wishing to join the KLA units. What would you do when people came who wanted to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: We took down their personal notes, information; that is, the names the places where they came from and so on. When we saw that they were not prepared to fight but they only wished to do, so we asked them to go back. When we saw that some of were resolute in their determination to fight we sent them to Voglushi, to Ymer, then to Qerqiz and they decided whether to accept these people or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they first sent to Voglushi and then to Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I said that some people knew Voglushi and they asked to meet him, specifically thinking that he would help -- he would make this easier for them to join the KLA. The number of people who wanted to join was great, and when they came to position number two, they came through the mountain path. It was was impossible for them to come through Komorane. They came through the mountains -- paths, through mountain paths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just need it clarify a little more what happened to these people after you saw them at position 2 because it's not absolutely clear and perhaps it's a translation problem, I'm not sure. When somebody came and you saw that they were ready to join the KLA, what would you do with that person? Who would you send that person to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: All of them who came there were willing and ready to fight. But some of them who insisted, more we sent them to the headquarters to Qerqiz, I said. Whereas when it came to people who knew Voglushi personally, they insisted on meeting him thinking that he would make it easier for them to join.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what would happen when these people were sent to Qerqiz? What would Qerqiz do, if you know?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: For some I know that they were admitted. Some others came again or went back for shortages of weapons. But most of them joined the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Qerqiz make the decision about whether they were admitted?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I think so. He was the person who decided. When there were weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when there were weapons? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I mean when there were reserves of weapons. Because in some instances people came with their own arms, weapons. And so they were admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You made a reference to a headquarters. Where was the headquarters in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: The headquarters changed premises in Lapusnik. It was always a small facility or place where Qerqiz and others stayed that we refer to as headquarters. But they moved to several places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember where the first place was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the houses located close to Guri 1 -- to Guri position, position number one. Then they moved to other places in the village or in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask with the assistance of the usher if you could be shown an aerial photograph of Lapusnik which we have marked as image 8 from P001. And if had a could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've seen this image before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be given a pen. And could you first -- are you oriented on this image?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, yes. On the basis of the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just point to the asphalt road for me.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: This one here. Can I mark it here? From here it continues, in this direction. It continues towards Peja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with the pen, could you first mark where position number one was, if you're able to find it?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Approximately, going by the hill it must be here. Can I mark it here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And if you could put a 1 there.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that position -- was that the only place of that position or did it extent in either direction down the hill?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It extended. New bunkers and trenches were dug in this part. Approximately in here. In a lower place and in a higher place. In two places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you draw with your pen the line of how far down that position 1 extended?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks] Approximately like this. But there were some other positions on a lower level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those other positions part position -- position number one?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the -- well, no. I'll move to a different question. Can you -- can you mark, please, if you're able to, where position number two was?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I think I was mistaken a little while ago. Position number one might have extended up to here, what I am drawing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could just reflect that the witness has drawn a line that goes from the number one towards the right of the -- of the diagram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you find position number two?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Position number two was here initially. Later there was a new position back there. And an old position of the Yugoslavia army that was situated here was used. So they became three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were three different bunkers at position 2. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. And they were connected with the trench. The last one went as far as here. It's a kind of valley there. The other part was also connected to other positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From position -- from any part of position number one was it possible to see the crossroads at Komorane?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: From Guri, no. From some close-by position, it was not possible. But when they were extended until here, yes. Here you could see. You could have a view of it, but not a full view. You couldn't see the Komorane peak. Only the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness indicated by pointing to the portion of the line that is near the number 1 that is -- well let me try and rephrase that. He pointed to the part of the line that is furthest from the number 1. But the line that I'm referring to is the line that is next to number one. I hope that is clear. Maybe -- well -- that is a good suggestion, to use the grid. The part of the line that he has pointed to is the part that is halfway between 488500 and 489000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you able to see position -- where position number three was on this map, or this image?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Position number three was very close to position number two, on this part here. Here I think there was a bunker and it continued up to here. Up to a certain field. I can't tell exactly when it was divided from position number four, which was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you put a 3 next to those two lines that you have drawn.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was position 4?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It must be approximately here. That must have been the position number four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 4 next to that.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you see position 5.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I see, but it was very close to the road that goes up to Berisa mountains. And I'm not capable of placing it exactly. It was approximately in this part here. And there was a guard which was positioned in the road towards "lugu" or the valley. This was the territory covered by position number five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now can you find on this diagram where the headquarters was first located. And maybe we could use a different colour pen now. Are you able to find first where the headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Must have been here. It was a place meant to be an old store, and here, in these houses here it was located. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just write HQ 1.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was the headquarters there, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Until the 29th of May. On the 29th of May, there was shelling at around 20, 21st hours [as interpreted] and these places were shelled. So they moved -- on the next day, they moved to another place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to find where they moved to?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. There is this circle here, in this part. In the house -- in the houses of Vojvoda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put HQ 2 there.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was the headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: For some days. Not for a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then where did the headquarters move to after that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: After that it moved to some houses, a compound of houses here. There was a big room, a big oda, it was initially used. After that a small house where a provisional clinic was installed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put HQ 3 there.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where the headquarters was up to the 26th of July?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, up to the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Qerqiz stay in these different headquarters?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The clinic that you refer to, was that next to or at the third headquarters that you have marked?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It was in the same courtyard with the headquarters. They both shared the same compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of clinic was it? What do you mean by "clinic"?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It was a small outpatient clinic there. Was a nurse and a doctor. It was one room to admit patients. Some shelves with medicaments. Not many but some that they could find.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able on this map to find where it was that you had the meeting where -- that you described where Fatmir Limaj said -- or Celiku said that Qerqiz would the person responsible for this position?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: No. It was in the beginning. It must have been here, in this place. It might be also somewhere in the vicinity of that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness pointed to what he has marked as HQ 1 when he said it was in this place or in the vicinity of this place.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I said here, in this part. HQ 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the other side of the road, of the Peja-Pristina road, were there other units?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: On the opposite side of the asphalt road, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were two other units on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of those units?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. Here was Pellumbi unit. On this part here. A little bit further was Guri unit, Guri 3 unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a P where the Pellumbi unit was and a G3 where the Guri 3 unit was.

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: [Marks] This must have been the place where the Guri -- Pellumbi unit was and here was the Guri unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below the -- in Lapusnik, below the Peja-Pristina road, was Celiku 3 the only unit that was there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: You mean on the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on the -- below the asphalt road in Lapusnik. Was Celiku 3 the only unit that was there?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: No, no. No. Above the asphalt road was our unit which patrolled. But there was a Pellumbi and this unit, the Pellumbi unit or the Guri unit, I'm not sure, they blocked the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- did the Pellumbi unit and the Guri unit control the road?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Up to Arlat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on your side of the Peja-Pristina road was it the Celiku 3 unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. On this side here were our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness pointed to the southern part of the Peja-Pristina road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, were the five possessions that you have identified, were they all within the Celiku 3 unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In -- was there another unit in Kishna Reka?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, in July. Not earlier. In July, a Pellumbi unit came. You couldn't see it on the map. There is a valley from position 5 down the hill. At the end of the hill there are some -- a group of houses, very close to each other. That was where the Pellumbi unit was located, with some 10 or 12 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there -- during June and July of 1998, was there a place in Lapusnik where soldiers would go to eat?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, there was. In June and July there was the kitchen here in this part where the circle is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness has pointed to the place where he marked HQ 2. And if that map could be given -- this image could be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P170. Under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. It does not need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in June and July of 1998 were there people who were in charge of these five fighting positions?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. Every position had someone who was in charge, who kept notes or who was responsible for changing the shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the occasions that you've talked about, were there other occasions when reports were made to Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: When something happened, each one could report individually. But not at a given time, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what kinds of things would be reported to Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: We reported on the situation in the position, what we had done in the way of building them. The movements of the enemy forces. Because usually they went by two, three armoured cars, APCs and tanks. And when they got together they started the attack. So we had to keep notes of the movements of a number of the enemy forces and tanks and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive orders from Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. Regarding the duties we were assigned, yes. About what -- when we were assigned to do something, to build something, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give any examples of orders?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: At first we didn't keep notes, but later we started keeping notes on some notebooks as I said earlier, about who was passing by, what was happening. I don't remember any specific orders or the changing of the guards, because first we didn't change -- we didn't take shifts, we stayed in the positions all day long. After the 22nd of May we changed in two shifts then at the end of June in three shifts and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he would give you orders -- when you had to build something. For example, what? Build what?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Some positions, what to do with that position. When we will to cut wood, for example wood that belong to the civilian population we had to agree what wood to cut or when we needed permission to go and visit our families. These were the topics that we discussed. Or when we lacked munitions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how you would get permission to go and visit your families?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: We asked for permission orally and when it was possible, we were allowed. That is, we were given a piece of paper and where it was indicated the place we were going to the time that we were staying there and so on. This was usually the case during these three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would give you permission?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'm going to show you a document. It's at tab 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were looking at the Albanian version of this document, and on the ELMO is the English version. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This was how these travel permits were organised or issued. This is how they were formulated. I think this is a little bit longer than what I used to but this is more or less it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would use these travel permits during June and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes. It was not possible to leave the position without having permission to leave it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on this -- this example there is a -- it's signed by a commander. In Lapusnik, would it be signed by Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: Yes, Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it can be taken off the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that another thing -- another subject that would be discussed was when you lacked munitions. What would you do if you lacked munitions?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: We asked the headquarters about it, and the headquarters conveyed our message, and then the munition came, whenever it was possible for it to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you asked the headquarters, what headquarters are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I was thinking about Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said "the headquarters conveyed our message." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: He had as one of his own tasks to go to Klecka and discuss those things. Our task was to go to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you asked Qerqiz for munitions? What -- after he conveyed the message, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: I said that he or it would come, the weapons or the munitions. Of course what we asked for was much more than what they could provide. The soldiers always asked for guns and munition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that reports -- notes and reports were kept at the positions. Can you tell the Court what kinds of things, if you can recall, were recorded in those notes and reports?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: It was a simple notebook where we wrote down the date; the shift, which shift was it the first, the second, or the third; the movement of the enemy forces; what had happen the during a certain shift; whose turn it was to have -- to be on a shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, was done with those reports or notes?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: When there was nothing important happening, nothing was done with it, until the notebook was filled and then it was handed over. Whenever there was something important happening we had to hand it over immediately. We notified --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- who did you notify?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: We had to notify Qerqizi and that's what we did. We notified him or sometimes Ymer. Because Qerqizi was not alone. He was with two or other three people [as interpreted]. So we could also notify these two or three people, and they would take care to take the news or this notification to Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify who those two or three other people were?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: During this time the people who stayed with Qerqizi was Ymeri, Katimi, Zeneli. Mesuesi slept somewhere else. But he used to -- to send written notes and documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the relationship between these people that you've just identified and Qerqizi?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: They were close. I don't know what their tasks were. It was never mentioned what their tasks were. With the exception that Zeneli for a period was responsible for point 3. With regard to Fatim, I don't know of any special tasks. He stayed with Qerqizi, Ymer stayed with Qerqizi and they slept at the state your name place where the headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you consider these people Zenel, Fatim and Ymeri to be at the same level as Qerqizi or at a different level?

utterances.speaker: Witness L-64
utterances.text: No. I said it earlier, that Qerqizi was responsible, but they were close. So they stayed together. Maybe they had free time to stay together with each other, and they slept at the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move into a different topic. Perhaps we could break a few minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, we will adjourn now for the day and will continue your evidence tomorrow at 2.15. If you would be kind enough to be back then. If I could just mention for the future planning and for the assistance of counsel with their travel moments that having regard to the need for travel and the difficulty that the forthcoming Easter break, we think it more practicable to finish sitting on Wednesday evening and not resume sitting on the Thursday and to, after Easter, commence sitting again on the Wednesday. At the moment, that is listed for Wednesday morning after Easter. It may that be that will be move to Wednesday afternoon depending on some other court-occupancy commitments. But I think with that arrangement it will be more feasible for people to make -- arrange the movements they need to make to get to their various homes and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I on behalf of the all of the travellers in the room thank the Tribunal very much for that indication. We're very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'll think of you on the Thursday while I'm here tending to other matters, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I hope I never far from Your Honour's thoughts. At any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Really. I'm glad to hear it. I need to be replaced by Mr. Guy-Smith, you see. We will adjourn now and resume at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
